Photograph: Kacper Pempel/Reuters Russia-Ukraine war at a glance Ukraine Explainer Ukraine war briefing: Cut-price Patriot among options in desperate search for missile defence Talks on Ukraine building Patriots continue despite Trump casting doubt, Reuters reports; forced evacuations in Kramatorsk. What we know on day 1,625 Warren Murray with Guardian writers and agencies Wed 5 Aug 2026 21.26 EDT Last modified on Wed 5 Aug 2026 21.27 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Ukraine could benefit from a Lockheed Martin project to build a new, lower-cost Patriot interceptor , the PAC-3 Adapted Capability Effector (ACE) missile , Reuters has reported. The news agency, citing defence and US government sources, said that despite Donald Trump casting doubt on a deal for Ukraine to build desperately needed Patriots, “no order was given to halt the discussions”, and talks continued with US arms makers, military officials and others. Ukraine has proven adept at producing large volumes of dramatically cheaper yet equally or more effective missiles and drones compared with those made by western allies. At least 17 people died on Wednesday as Kyiv again came under heavy Russian bombardment . Ukrainian forces, starved of suitable interceptors, were unable to shoot down a single missile . A US official told Reuters that the most feasible option for Patriots would be making some components in Ukraine and assembling them in Germany , where an older Patriot model is already made and the more advanced PAC-3 is expected to be produced as well. Trump has raised security concerns about handing over highly secretive Patriot blueprints in their entirety to Ukraine. 1:19 Deadly overnight Russian missile attack sparks fires across Kyiv – video Any plan for Ukraine to be involved in Patriot production could still take a year or more to come to fruition , officials have cautioned, with new component lines typically not up and running until three to seven years after a licensing deal is signed. Lockheed Martin suggested an accelerated timeline for Patriot PAC-3 ACE in an announcement on 20 July , emphasising that the use of the same launchers and software would speed up development. The interceptors would cost less than half of a normal Patriot missile, it claimed. Germany’s interior minister warned of “a new level of danger” after a drone carrying explosives was found at Leipzig airport, while a DHL plane in flight was hit by a flying object. German police used a bomb disposal robot to defuse and destroy the explosive device. Deborah Cole and Andrew Roth write that suspicion has fallen on Russia given the airport’s status as a Nato and German military logistics hub, and as the base for Ukraine’s Antonov Airlines in Europe. The quadcopter fitted with an explosive device was found near a Ukrainian Antonov cargo plane , according to media reports. The Leipzig drone bomb marks a dangerous escalation for Europe Read more Vladimir Tkachuk, the head of Russian drone manufacturer Uraldronzavod , was critically injured in a car bombing , in what appeared to be the latest in a series of assassination attempts targeting figures linked to the country’s war in Ukraine, Pjotr Sauer writes . A bomb planted beneath his Mercedes exploded, according to Russian state media, killing his bodyguard. On Saturday an explosion outside an upmarket restaurant in central Moscow killed five people. Col Gen Aleksandr Chayko, the commander of Russia’s aerospace forces, was reportedly celebrating his birthday at the restaurant. Ukrainian authorities have ordered hundreds of families with children to leave the city of Kramatorsk in eastern Ukraine because of intensifying Russian strikes. Russian forces are within 20km (12 miles) of the city’s eastern edge, according to DeepState, a war monitor close to the Ukrainian army. A total of 525 children and their guardians are being forcibly evacuated. Kramatorsk is part of the “fortress belt” that Ukraine’s troops are fighting to hold. Russia’s Saratov refinery stopped processing crude oil on 2 August after ⁠a Ukrainian drone attack damaged production facilities and triggered fires at the plant owned by ⁠the country’s ⁠largest ​oil company Rosneft, two industry sources told Reuters. They said the refinery’s CDU-6 crude ‌distillation unit, its ‌only crude processing unit, was shut down. The unit, with a nominal capacity of 20,000 tonnes of oil per day, could take between two and three weeks to repair. Russia’s imports of gasoline and diesel from Belarus surged in July because of Ukrainian strikes disabling Russian oil refineries, according to calculations by Reuters. https://www.delfi.lt/en/politics/lithuan.text: Delfi EN Delfi Politics 2026.08.13 17:38 Lithuania sends 20 more border guards to assist Latvia Translated by Karolis Broga Source: Elta EN Lithuania sends 20 more border guards to assist Latvia PHOTO: Andrius Ufartas | Elta Follow Delfi on Google As Latvia faces an influx of irregular migrants from the territory of Belarus, the State Border Guard Service of Lithuania (VSAT) on Wednesday sent another group of border guards to assist Latvian officers, the Ministry of the Interior has announced. According to the ministry, in coordination of Latvian officers, Lithuanian border guards carry out border surveillance, prevent irregular migration and perform other tasks related to state border protection. The group sent to Latvia consists of 20 Lithuanian border guards. On Thursday, Minister of the Interior Martynas Katelynas also awarded commendations to 27 VSAT officers who have already returned from their mission in Latvia, where they helped guard the European Union’s external border. The minister stressed that the security of Lithuania and Latvia is closely interconnected, therefore, assistance to the neighbouring country is an important example of a joint response to illegal migration. According to the Ministry of the Interior, this year Latvia has prevented 9,675 irregular migrants from crossing the border from Belarus, compared with 1,105 migrants stopped at the Lithuanian border with Belarus. Last year, 1,288 irregular migrants transported from Latvia or travelling from Latvia independently were detained in Lithuania. Whereas in the first half of 2026 alone, 1,546 migrants have already been detained after entering Lithuania from Latvia. After illegally crossing the Latvia–Belarus border, they attempted to reach Western Europe via Lithuania and Poland. https://www.politico.eu/article/france-d.text: PARIS — France is open to cooperating with Sweden on building a next-generation fighter jet, an Elysée official told reporters on Friday. "We're both looking for aircraft that are fairly similar, fairly small," the French official said, speaking ahead of President Emmanuel Macron's visit to the Nordic country Monday. "In response to the question: Are there any avenues for cooperation? Of course, there are many: we have aircraft engine production capacity that Sweden doesn’t have — that’s something we could cooperate on," they added. Advertisement Advertisement The French comments are the clearest overture made to Stockholm since the high-profile failure of a next-generation fighter jet project between France, Germany and Spain, known as the Future Combat Air System (FCAS). The decade-long program faltered due to disagreements between France's Dassault Aviation and Germany's Airbus Defence and Space, and ultimately collapsed last spring. The competition between Paris and Berlin to attract Stockholm is one of the most closely watched developments in the aerospace sector. POLITICO previously reported that Germany had already reached out to Sweden. The Nordic country's defense champion Saab makes its own fourth-generation Gripen fighter — although the warplane's engine uses core technology from American company GE Aerospace. Engines for France's Rafale fighter jets are locally made by Safran. "Dassault builds its own aircraft, and Saab builds its own: two competitors with fairly similar approaches who respect one another. There was cooperation in the past," the official said, stressing however that "nothing formal has been agreed" on fighter jet cooperation. Sweden is expected to decide on the next steps for its warplane program by September 2027.

https://www.politico.eu/article/gordon-b.text: LIVERPOOL, England — Former U.K. Prime Minister Gordon Brown recently insisted he does not want to become “a backseat driver” telling Andy Burnham’s new government what to do. But it seems he just can’t help himself. A succession of cabinet ministers and other leading Labour politicians have told POLITICO that Brown, a party elder who was prime minister between 2007 and 2010, contacts them by email — written in capital letters — to offer them advice. And on Tuesday, Burnham, who has been PM for just 10 weeks, disclosed that he is looking to emulate Brown, heaping praise on his predecessor for showing how Britain could lead the world through a crisis. Advertisement Advertisement “As Gordon Brown has said, we can be the world’s innovation nation, and he’s right, we can,” Burnham told Labour’s conference on Tuesday, saying the U.K. could be “an honest broker” in the debate on regulating AI. “Just as Gordon did in the financial crisis in 2008, so Britain will do it again — step forward, and bring people together around what’s right for the future — securing our prosperity, but also our safety.” Burnham served in Brown’s government as health secretary until Labour lost power in 2010. He has picked colleagues who served with him in Brown’s ministerial team for key jobs in government — including Ed Miliband, the new foreign secretary, Chancellor John Healey, and Douglas Alexander, the Scotland secretary. In interviews at the POLITICO Pub during Labour’s conference in Liverpool this week, the extent of Brown’s contacts became clear. Miliband, who was an adviser to Brown during his time in the Treasury, said they had spoken by phone while he was in New York at the U.N. General Assembly earlier this month. “I had a late-night phone call with him actually last week,” Miliband said. “They come thick and fast. It’s a great email to get, honestly.” Healey, the chancellor, disclosed in an interview with the Sunday Times that he receives emails in bold capitals from Brown, who was Britain’s longest-serving chancellor of modern times, before he became prime ministers in 2007. Alexander, the Scotland secretary, told POLITICO he, too, was the recipient of messages from Brown, who represented a Scottish constituency during his time in parliament. “Yes, it took me great restraint when John Healey revealed that he was receiving emails in Bold Helvetica 14, as I remember, from Gordon Brown, not to send him a message saying ‘the first 35 years is the worst, and then you get over it.’” Advertisement Advertisement New Scottish Labour leader Michael Marra also revealed in a POLITICO Pub interview that he’d been in receipt of emailed advice from Brown, “sometimes in caps, sometimes not.” Marra is clearly a fan of the former premier: “He’s a constant force for good, and I feel very privileged every time I get an email from him,” he said. Healey also told Labour members in Liverpool that he once had to lend Brown a red tie for his speech to the Labour Party conference in 1999. Brown returned it afterwards, and signed it, and Healey said he had kept it safe ever since, until he put it on again on Monday to deliver his own conference speech as chancellor. Brown, whose office did not immediately respond to a request for comment, does have an official government role: Burnham has kept him on as an adviser on global finance and cooperation, a post he was given by the previous PM, Keir Starmer. In that role, Brown is due to contribute to developing “new international finance partnerships that can support defence and security-related investment, including measures that underpin the U.K.’s relationship with Europe,” according to the government press release announcing his appointment. Brown’s role is officially “unpaid” and “part time,” although that hasn’t stopped him working late to contact ministers after hours. Andrew McDonald, John Johnston and Dan Bloom contributed reporting from Liverpool.

https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq98.text: Image source, PA Media By Becky Morton ,Â Political reporter Â and Â Jennifer McKiernan ,Â Political reporter Published 13 October 2026 Updated 5 hours ago Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he will try to "repair bridges" between Ukraine and the United States, ahead of a meeting with President Volodymyr Zelensky at Downing Street. The Ukrainian president was welcomed by a military ceremonial guard outside Number 10 as he arrived for the meeting, in what is thought to be a first for a foreign leader. It comes after President Donald Trump said he had struck a deal with Moscow to import Russian diesel. Asked about Trump's move during Prime Minister's Questions, Burnham resisted criticising the US president, saying he wanted to "be careful in terms of laying the ground to bring people back together". However, he stressed that Zelensky would not be leaving the UK "empty-handed", as he said further military and financial support would be drawn up in the coming weeks. Burnham is expected to use the visit to promise further sanctions against Russia, while also announcing the UK will accelerate its delivery of air defence missiles to Kyiv. The UK will also urge allies to step up pressure on Russia, with Chancellor John Healey using International Monetary Fund meetings to call for a ban on Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG). It is Zelensky's second visit to the UK since Burnham became prime minister. While other world leaders have received military welcomes, Number 10 said it could not find a record of one taking place on Downing Street. Image source, Reuters Image caption, The King held an audience with President Zelensky at Buckingham Palace as part of his visit to the UK During PMQs, Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey asked whether he agreed the diesel deal was "yet another shameful Trump betrayal of the Ukrainian people and European security". In response, Burnham did not echo Sir Ed's condemnation of Trump, saying: "What I have to do in my role is try and repair bridges so that the support comes back and therefore I should at this moment in time be careful in terms of laying the ground to bring people back together." The PM said he had spoken to Zelensky over the phone on Saturday "because I recognised it was another very dark and difficult moment for him as they contemplate a winter that will be severe for his people". The phone call came after Trump announced that President Vladimir Putin had agreed to release millions of tonnes of Russian diesel into the US, as he suspended sanctions on diesel from Moscow. Zelensky branded the move a gift to Putin, warning it would provide Moscow with money to continue its war against Ukraine. Trump responded by saying it was "time for Ukraine to get a new president" . Meanwhile, Zelensky has said at least 600,000 people across Ukraine were left without electricity after deadly overnight Russian missile and drone strikes . He said "critical" energy infrastructure had been hit â despite Trump's claim on Sunday that a ceasefire on strikes on energy infrastructure was in place between Russia and Ukraine. Russia said its strikes had hit communications and energy facilities used by Ukraine's military. Zelensky has said Ukraine is ready to halt its strikes on Russian oil refineries and other energy facilities if Moscow did the same. But Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov has said Ukraine does not deserve the "respite" a ceasefire would bring. https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/world-leaders-.text: World leaders and politicians took to social media to post tributes to the victims of the Hamas attack three years ago. The Prime Minister of Israel's account on X also posted a LEGO video appearing to explain the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.'Three years on from the October 7 attacks on Israel, we remember those who were senselessly killed by Hamas terrorists. The impact of the attacks has been felt not just in Israel, but in Jewish communities across the world who still bear the burden of the tragic events that day,' said UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham.Protection for Jewish SpacesAccording to the Israeli Foreign Ministry, 1,200 people, comprising of Israelis and foreign nationals, were killed during the 7 October 2023 Hamas attack and around 250 were taken hostage. Burnham has pledged to come down hard on antisemitism and announced funding for the protection of synagogues, schools, and community buildings.Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, for his part, enumerated the Canadians who lost their lives in the attack. 'Canada unequivocally condemns Hamas, which must play no role in the future governance of a demilitarised Palestinian state,' he said.Countries including the UK and Canada have called for a two-state solution to end the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. European Council President António Costa also said that the two-state solution is the only 'viable path to a just and lasting peace in the Middle East.'Memorial Candle for the VictimsIsraeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu lit a memorial candle in his office in Jerusalem to commemorate the victims of the Hamas attack. 'The nation unites on this day in the longing for our dear ones. We will complete the mission: we have settled the score and will continue settling the score with all the murderers,' he said on social media.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who is no stranger to war, also shared his condolences and sorrow: 'No other act of terror and no other war of aggression rooted in hatred should be forgiven or forgotten. There have already been far too many killings in the 21st century, a century that should have been, and must still become, entirely different.'Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten remembered the chaos that descended in Israel and Palestine following the Hamas attack. 'The region descended into a spiral of conflict and misery. Tens of thousands of innocent Palestinians have been killed by the Israeli army since the Hamas attack,' he said.Many American politicians and officials shared words of remembrance. President Donald Trump said on Truth Social: I fought relentlessly to bring the hostages home, and reunite them with their loved ones, and I did, both the living and the dead!French President Emmanuel Macron also remembered the 51 French nationals who died on 7 October 2023. He said: 'Combating antisemitism and terrorism, everywhere and always, working for peace and the security of all: that is France's commitment.'UN Secretary-General António Guterres has called for a permanent ceasefire, respect for international law and implementation of the Comprehensive Plan to End the Gaza Conflict.Romanian President Nicușor Dan echoed the need for a permanent ceasefire: 'Romania stands behind the Board of Peace and has opened its hospitals to children from Gaza. The fragile ceasefire must become a lasting settlement, one that gives Israelis security and Palestinians a state of their own.'
